summary: Backend-only tests for Research Run. 11/11 pytest tests passed in ~73s including the primary bug-fix scenario: uploaded /tmp/mtech.pdf, started SSE analysis, disconnected the client after 7s, then polled /api/paper/{id} until status='completed'. Verified analysis.summary.tldr, score.paper_score>0, gaps>=1, questions>=1, final_report>500 chars. SSE resume also verified (workflow_start + workflow_done/__end__ replayed).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py stats endpoint iterates over analyses to compute counts; fine for now but for large scale, MongoDB aggregation would be preferable.
agents.py _JOBS is an in-memory dict — background workflows are lost on backend restart. Consider persisting job state so an interrupted analysis can resume from DB after a restart.

subscribe() is an async generator; if a paper_id has no job registered, it silently returns (empty stream). Endpoint always starts a job when none exists so OK, but consider returning 404 in edge cases.
AnalysisResult model unused in _build_analysis_doc — doc is built as a raw dict; consider using the pydantic model for validation.
load_dotenv is called with explicit ROOT_DIR / '.env' — good.
seed_data_creation: Uploaded /tmp/mtech.pdf during test; deleted at the end via test_delete_paper.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file /app/backend/tests/test_research_run.py is idempotent — each run uploads mtech.pdf, runs full 10-agent analysis (~60-90s Groq real-time), then deletes the paper. Uses pytest-xdist with --junitxml. BASE_URL from REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Groq free tier TPM limits could cause flakiness under load; observed successful run in 73s.
rca of the issue: Bug fix confirmed: analysis workflow runs as a detached asyncio Task in agents.py::start_workflow keyed on paper_id in _JOBS. SSE endpoint only subscribes to broadcasts; disconnecting the SSE client removes the subscriber queue but the background task keeps running and persists via on_agent_done/on_complete callbacks. Final status transitions uploaded -> analyzing -> completed as expected.
